result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.from_edges()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: Build a new graph from an edge list. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.from_edges()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: Build a new graph from an edge list. title: >- [Graph.from_edges()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Build a new graph from an edge list. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Build a new graph from an edge list. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L2261-L2435){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.from_edges( edges, directed=False, weighted=None, nodes=None, graph_name=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Graph from edges](../assets/graphs/from-edges.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Left: a card with the edge list, four (source, target, weight) tuples: A to B 2, A to C 1, B to D 3 and C to D 4, and below it nodes equal to the list with E, in the accent color. Right: the new weighted graph, a four-cycle A, B, D, C with each weight on its edge, every endpoint made a node, and the isolated node E, which only nodes= names, in the accent color beside it." width="100%"} The quickest way to turn a list of pairs into a graph: every endpoint becomes a node, in order of first appearance, so there's no need to create the nodes first or to pass `auto_create_nodes=True`. It's EdgeCase's version of NetworkX's `Graph(edge_list)` and igraph's `Graph.TupleList()`. The edge items have the same shapes as in `add_edges()`: `(source, target)`, `(source, target, weight)`, `(source, target, attrs)` and `(source, target, weight, attrs)`, where a dict's `"weight"` key also sets the weight and its `"rel"` key the relationship type. The rows of a NumPy array work too (as an array has one dtype, whole-number floats in its first two columns count as integers). Every endpoint is a node *label*, not a node ID: values that aren't strings are converted with `str()`, so `[(0, 1), (1, 2)]` gives nodes labeled `"0"`, `"1"` and `"2"` (and `1` and `"1"` are the same node). Repeated pairs make parallel edges and `(a, a)` makes a self-loop. The whole build is recorded as a single step (see `steps`). ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [edges]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The edges, as a list (or any iterable) of tuples or lists, or a NumPy array with two or three columns. [directed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether the graph is directed. Default is `False`. [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[bool]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether the graph is weighted. If `None` (the default), it is when any edge has a weight. [nodes]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[list, dict, None]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional nodes to create first, in the forms `add_nodes()` accepts: a list of labels or `(label, attrs)` tuples, or a dict mapping each label to its attributes. Use it to add isolated nodes, to give nodes attributes, or to fix the node order (and so the node IDs). Endpoints not listed are added after these. [graph_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional name for the graph. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A new graph holding the nodes and edges. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [TypeError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If an edge isn't one of the accepted shapes or has a weight that isn't a number, or a node's attributes aren't a dict. [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If an endpoint is `None`, an edge gives its weight twice, or `nodes=` lists a label more than once. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} A list of pairs is all it takes: ::: {#1c299e0d .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph.from_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "A"), ("C", "D")]) graph ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` Number of nodes : 4 Number of edges : 4 Directed : False Density : 0.67 Average degree (min, max) : 2.00 (1, 3) Connected : True Number of connected components : 1 Tree : False Bipartite : False ``` ::: ::: A number as the third element is the edge's weight, and the graph is weighted because some edge has one: ::: {#bd16faa1 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} roads = ec.Graph.from_edges( [("Oslo", "Bergen", 463), ("Oslo", "Trondheim", 494), ("Bergen", "Trondheim", 633)] ) roads.get_edges_str_repr(use_labels=True), roads.get_edge_df()["weight"].to_list() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` (['Oslo--Bergen', 'Oslo--Trondheim', 'Bergen--Trondheim'], [463.0, 494.0, 633.0]) ``` ::: ::: Integers become labels, and `nodes=` adds a node that no edge mentions: ::: {#5c07a04f .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} g = ec.Graph.from_edges([(0, 1), (1, 2)], directed=True, nodes=[0, 1, 2, 3]) g.get_node_df().select(["id", "label"]), g.get_edges_str_repr(use_labels=True) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` (shape: (4, 2) ┌─────┬───────┐ │ id ┆ label │ │ --- ┆ --- │ │ i64 ┆ str │ ╞═════╪═══════╡ │ 1 ┆ 0 │ │ 2 ┆ 1 │ │ 3 ┆ 2 │ │ 4 ┆ 3 │ └─────┴───────┘, ['0->1', '1->2']) ``` ::: ::: Attribute dicts become edge attributes, and `nodes=` can give nodes theirs: ::: {#a2b18698 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} g = ec.Graph.from_edges( [("ann", "bob", {"rel": "friend", "since": 2019}), ("bob", "cat", {"rel": "boss"})], nodes={"ann": {"age": 31}, "cat": {"age": 45}}, ) g.get_node_df().select(["label", "age"]), g.get_edge_df().select(["rel", "since"]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` (shape: (3, 2) ┌───────┬──────┐ │ label ┆ age │ │ --- ┆ --- │ │ str ┆ i64 │ ╞═══════╪══════╡ │ ann ┆ 31 │ │ cat ┆ 45 │ │ bob ┆ null │ └───────┴──────┘, shape: (2, 2) ┌────────┬───────┐ │ rel ┆ since │ │ --- ┆ --- │ │ str ┆ i64 │ ╞════════╪═══════╡ │ friend ┆ 2019 │ │ boss ┆ null │ └────────┴───────┘) ``` ::: :::
